Fazlur Rahman and others
Vs.
Anjab Khan being dead his heirs Haji Md. Manir Khan & Ors.
full_judgment: 6. Mr. Kazi Mozzammelul Huq with, Mr. M.A. Gaffer, the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the petitioner submitted that both the courts below committed serious error of law in passing their judgments and decrees in not appreciating the settled principle of law that the plaintiff was to succeed on the basis of his own evidence and not on the witnesses of the other side if any., He further, submitted that both the Courts on misreading and non-reading the oral and documentary evidence disbelieved the case of the defendant No. 1. He further argued that both the courts below failed to appreciate the proof of defendants title by of pattan, kabala, Bainapatra and all the evidence on his side proved the said facts and also the possession of defendant No.1. Both the courts below misdirected themselves in holding a ground that the plaintiff failed to state specifying the suit land and further the failed to appreciate the provision as laid town in section 30 of State Acquisition of Tenancy Act of 1950. He finally argued that the plain-tiffs opposite party completely failed to prove possession followed by dispossession by any sufficient oral and documentary evidence. In support of his contention he referred the case of Imanuddin Barbi vs. Lilabati Das, reported in 32 DLR-75, Sultan Ahmed vs. Md. Waziullah and others, reported in 7 BLD-235, Munshi Dudhu in and others vs. Rahimuddin and others, reported in 16 DLR 56, Barada Prasanna Lod and others, vs. Kobbad Mia, reported in 13 DLR-765, The Crown vs. Mongal Khan, reported in 6 DLR-490.
